entries.sourceTitle: Extension of timeline with respect to compliance of Digital Accessibility Circulars
entries.previousRequirement: SEBI's 31 July 2026 extension had set 31 October 2026 for accessibility audits of digital platforms and remediation. The earlier extension did not include the new wording expressly extending IAAP auditor appointment.
entries.newRequirement: Appointment of an IAAP auditor, accessibility audit of digital platforms and remediation of audit findings are extended to 31 January 2027. All other provisions of the earlier digital-accessibility circulars remain unchanged.
entries.applicabilityAssessment: Circular addressed all Registered Intermediaries and AMFI. Luxmi InvestCare is AMFI-registered as an MFD; direct applicability to this individual distributor website, as distinct from SEBI-registered intermediaries/AMFI, requires human confirmation. Treat as potentially applicable and complete accessibility assessment promptly.

risk.reason: Potential regulated accessibility obligations and a 69-day deadline from the retrieval date; no accessibility audit evidence was found in the repository audit.

impactedFilesRoutes: all 13 public routes listed in compliance/audit/latest.json
app/admin/* (internal authenticated interface; not in public route probe)
entries.aiAnalysis: The date extension does not remove the underlying accessibility obligations. Existing audit probes test route availability and compliance language, not accessibility. The current repository has no evidence of an IAAP audit or a dedicated automated accessibility test. Do not treat HTTP 200 responses or a successful build as accessibility compliance. A human must confirm scope and arrange an IAAP auditor where applicable.
entries.changeSummary: No website code or content change made in this run because legal scope and a formal accessibility audit require professional review. Added official accessibility circular to the watch source configuration and recorded a remediation checklist in the durable log.
validationEvidence: Official SEBI circular and PDF reviewed; primary source confirms 31 January 2027 deadline and that all other provisions remain unchanged.
Repository inspection found no accessibility audit/test evidence. This is a gap observation, not a completed accessibility audit.
unresolvedQuestions: Confirm whether Luxmi InvestCare as AMFI-registered MFD is directly within the SEBI circular's 'Registered Intermediaries' scope or otherwise covered through AMFI.
Who will appoint an IAAP auditor and confirm audit/remediation coverage for public and internal digital platforms?
entries.historicalEntry: The 31 July 2026 SEBI circular had extended accessibility audit and remediation to 31 October 2026. The 30 October 2026 circular further extended the relevant tasks to 31 January 2027 and expressly included appointment of an IAAP auditor.

entries.sourceTitle: Digital Personal Data Protection Rules, 2025 (G.S.R. 846(E)) and commencement notification G.S.R. 843(E)
entries.effectiveDate: Rule 4: 2026-11-13 (one-year commencement). Rules 3, 5-16, 22 and 23: 2027-05-13 (calculated 18 months from Gazette date).
entries.previousRequirement: DPDP Act and Rules commencement was phased by G.S.R. 843(E) and Rule 1 of G.S.R. 846(E); obligations did not all commence on a single date.
entries.newRequirement: Rule 4 (Consent Manager registration and obligations) is effective from 13 November 2026. The principal notice, security, rights, breach and other Data Fiduciary rule package listed in Rules 3, 5-16, 22 and 23 is scheduled to commence 13 May 2027, calculated from the Gazette date. The exact commencement schedule should be read from the Gazette, including amendments/corrigenda.
entries.applicabilityAssessment: Luxmi's website collects enquiry details and uses report-sharing/browser storage, but current repository inspection did not identify a Consent Manager service. Rule 4 is not a direct website obligation on the facts currently observed. Future Data Fiduciary requirements are material because personal data is processed through enquiry/report-share journeys.

risk.reason: Upcoming privacy obligations with a May 2027 commencement date; current privacy notice describes data and purposes but does not specify a fixed retention period.

impactedFilesRoutes: lead APIs/database and admin lead access
entries.aiAnalysis: The current privacy page, last updated 6 October 2026, describes enquiry fields (name, phone, email, message, source page), report-sharing session data/localStorage, processing purposes, consent withdrawal contact, security and a flexible retention statement. Future Rule 3 requires a clear standalone notice with itemised personal data, specific purposes and accessible means to withdraw consent, exercise rights and complain to the Board. A gap analysis should verify these elements, retention, processor roles, rights workflow and incident response before commencement. Do not assume Rule 4 makes Luxmi a Consent Manager.
entries.changeSummary: No privacy policy or consent-flow code change made because implementation and legal choices require review. Added official MeitY DPDP Rules index and Gazette references to the watch configuration and logged a preparation checklist.
validationEvidence: Official DPDP Rules Gazette G.S.R. 846(E) reviewed: Rule 4 one-year commencement and Rules 3, 5-16, 22, 23 eighteen-month commencement.
Official commencement notification G.S.R. 843(E) reviewed; calendar dates calculated from 13 November 2025 publication.
Privacy policy code inspected; no privacy-specific automated test run in this session.
unresolvedQuestions: Confirm data retention periods for enquiry records, report-sharing history and any analytics.
Confirm processors/vendors, consent bases, data rights request handling, breach-response responsibilities and whether consent is collected for each relevant processing purpose.
Have legal/privacy reviewer approve notice and implementation plan before 13 May 2027.

entries.authority: CERT-In / Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology
entries.sourceTitle: Abuse of Business Payment Workflows and Use of AI-Driven Agentic Offensive Frameworks across Sectors (CIAD-2026-0062)
entries.effectiveDate: No separate statutory commencement date; advisory recommendations should be assessed and acted on promptly.
entries.previousRequirement: Prior CERT-In advisories CIAD-2026-0046, 0049 and 0058 covered payment/disbursement API abuse and AI-enabled intrusions. Existing main-branch login and public enquiry APIs were not protected by visible application-level rate-limit calls in the inspected routes; the remediation proposal remains unmerged.
entries.newRequirement: CIAD-2026-0062 (Critical advisory) describes misuse of trusted business workflows and underlying records/approval relationships, AI-driven agentic offensive frameworks, automated reconnaissance, credential attacks and unauthorized access. It advises reviewing exposed applications/APIs, identities, privileged accounts, service credentials, external interfaces, monitoring and incident response; see the advisory for references and applicable incident-reporting guidance.
entries.applicabilityAssessment: Payment/disbursement workflow abuse is not directly evidenced in Luxmi's current repository: no payment/payout/disbursement filenames or route names were found in the recursive tree search. The general credential, exposed-application/API, privileged-access, CRM record-change and AI-agent intrusion risks are relevant because the website has login, public lead-submission and authenticated admin/CRM endpoints. No evidence of compromise was identified; no incident/log investigation was performed.

risk.reason: CERT-In classifies the advisory as Critical. Luxmi's current evidenced exposure is elevated but not assessed Critical because payment/disbursement processing was not identified; authentication abuse and unauthorized lead/CRM access or changes remain relevant.

entries.aiAnalysis: Read-only inspection of main shows validated login input and bcrypt password comparison, but no visible rate-limit call in the login route; the public lead endpoint validates input and consent but has no visible rate-limit call. Inspected admin APIs use getCurrentUser/role checks and parameterized SQL, but privileged record changes, session/cookie protections, logging and operational monitoring require a deeper review. Main next.config.ts has no response-security headers in the inspected version. PR #17 proposes login/lead rate limiting and response headers, but it remains open/unmerged and its last known CI build/deployment validation failed. The advisory does not by itself establish that Luxmi operates payment workflows or require a specific code change. A safe next step is review/validate the existing PR #17 mitigation rather than duplicating or making untested changes.
entries.changeSummary: No application code changed. Created human-review issue #20 and added two CERT-In monitoring sources (2026 advisory listing and CIAD-2026-0062 detail) to the existing regulatory-watch PR branch.
validationEvidence: Official CERT-In advisory page CIAD-2026-0062 opened and reviewed; it states Original Issue Date 20 Nov 2026 and severity Critical.
Current main login route, public leads route, selected authenticated admin routes, next.config.ts, and recursive repository tree were inspected through read-only GitHub retrieval.
Repository tree search for payment/payout/disbursement/transfer/bank/invoice filename terms returned no matches; this is a filename/path search, not proof of absence of payment code.

Main weekly audit #84 (run 45405885027) completed with final gate failure; compliance scan, dependency audit, build, route probe/report steps completed, but audit status remained FAIL. The report records production vulnerabilities (3: 1 critical, 1 high, 1 low), full-tree vulnerabilities (6: 1 critical, 1 high, 3 moderate, 1 low), high promotional-language finding on /calculators/sip, and 13/13 routes HTTP 200.
PR #17 is open/unmerged; last known CI workflow #46 failed at production build and route audit was skipped. Rate-limit/header proposal is not active in main.
JSON/source config validated by parsing in automation before GitHub update. No local npm audit, ESLint, TypeScript, build, penetration test, production test or log review was run.
unresolvedQuestions: Confirm whether Luxmi has any payment, disbursement, payout, banking or external vendor workflows not represented in public repository paths.
Review and validate rate-limit design, migration, trusted-proxy/IP handling and security headers in PR #17; diagnose build failure and rerun CI.
Confirm admin MFA, least-privilege service credentials, secrets hygiene, privileged record-change auditability, and incident response procedures.
If compromise is suspected, investigate logs and follow applicable CERT-In incident reporting directions; this review found no evidence of compromise but did not examine logs.

entries.sourceTitle: Simplification of client on-boarding and rationalisation of risk management framework at KYC Registration Agencies — Circular HO/38/14/(25)2026-MIRSD-POD3
entries.effectiveDate: 2026-12-24 (30 days from issuance, as stated in the circular). KRAs must issue an implementation SOP within 30 days from circular issuance.
entries.previousRequirement: The KYC Master Circular and KRA framework governed client onboarding, supplementary information, updates, verification, portability and delinking; the circular revises several of those provisions and data flows.
entries.newRequirement: The circular centralises common supplementary KYC information; requires relevant uploads including income range, FATCA/CRS, PEP, occupation, CKYC ID/DIGIPIN where available and OVD expiry as applicable; tags independently validated information; requires updating KYC records from KRA/CKYCRR updates and a client option to confirm; makes mobile verification optional if KRA already tags an Aadhaar-seeded number verified; revises closure/non-association/delinking timelines; permits optional overseas address proof for certain resident OCI/foreign-national clients with verified Indian address; revises name-change evidence; and enhances validated-record portability/attribute tagging. Detailed circular text and exceptions control.
entries.applicabilityAssessment: Circular is addressed to SEBI-registered intermediaries, KRAs, exchanges, clearing corporations and depositories. Luxmi is AMFI-registered as an MFD and may participate in KYC workflows through AMCs/RTA/KRA; direct applicability and actual workflow duties need confirmation. Public site routes inspected contain enquiry/contact forms, not a direct KYC/account-opening or document-upload journey.

risk.reason: Effective 24 December 2026, close to this review; MFD business onboarding/KYC processes may be affected if Luxmi participates.
